content.value_statement: Distributed Rust systems need tests that cover logic, async behavior, synchronization, and parser safety. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for Guts testing.
actual_capabilities: Shows a testing pyramid for balancing unit, integration, end-to-end, property, and fuzz tests.
Provides Rust unit test patterns with grouped tests and clear assertions.
Demonstrates async and multi-node integration test structures for Guts repositories.
Introduces property-based tests with proptest and fuzz targets with cargo-fuzz.
Lists common Cargo test, coverage, benchmark, and fuzzing commands.
Shows CI matrix and mock dependency patterns for Rust projects.
limitations: Examples are templates and may need imports, types, or helpers from the local Guts codebase.
The skill focuses on Rust and Guts, so other languages need adaptation.
It does not generate full project fixtures without repository context.
Fuzzing and benchmark commands can take significant local compute time.

use_cases.title: Add Unit Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Use the unit test patterns to organize repository tests and validate error handling.

use_cases.title: Validate Distributed Sync
use_cases.description: Model multi-node integration tests that create, connect, and verify repository synchronization.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Parser Reliability
use_cases.description: Apply property-based testing and fuzzing patterns to find crashes and invariant failures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one focused unit test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing skill to write a Rust unit test for this Guts function. Include the success case and one invalid input case.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Test Modules
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a maintainable test layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing skill to propose a test module structure for these repository behaviors. Group related tests and name each case clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Design Integration Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for async and multi-node behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing skill to design integration tests for repository creation, cloning, node connection, and synchronization across three nodes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Property and Fuzz Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for reliability testing of critical inputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing skill to create property-based test ideas and fuzz targets for this parser or identity component. Explain the invariants to verify.

output_examples.input: I need tests for repository name validation.
output_examples.output: A concise test plan with valid names, empty names, invalid characters, boundary lengths, and grouped Rust test cases.

output_examples.input: I need confidence that three nodes sync repositories.
output_examples.output: An integration test outline that starts test nodes, connects them, creates a repository, waits for sync, and verifies all nodes.

output_examples.input: I need stronger parser safety checks.
output_examples.output: A property and fuzzing plan that defines parser invariants, random input coverage, panic checks, and expected failure handling.

best_practices: Start with many focused unit tests before adding slower integration or end-to-end tests.
Keep async tests bounded with timeouts so failures do not hang the test suite.
Use property tests and fuzz targets for parsers, signatures, and other input-heavy logic.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on end-to-end tests for core repository behavior.
Do not leave multi-node tests dependent on uncontrolled timing or shared state.
Do not run long fuzzing or benchmark jobs without clear limits in local workflows.

faq.question: What projects is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for Guts and similar Rust distributed systems that need reliable test coverage.

faq.question: Does the skill include runnable tests?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples. You must adapt names, imports, fixtures, and helpers to your repository.

faq.question: Can it help with async Rust tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes tokio test patterns, timeout guidance, and multi-node integration examples.

faq.question: Does it cover fuzzing?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows cargo-fuzz usage and a parser fuzz target pattern for crash resistance.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it replace project-specific test design?
faq.answer: No. It gives reusable testing strategies, but local architecture and risk areas still drive final coverage.
